title: Pattern
description:
A shape observed at two or more distinct scales. The ledger records what happened to the store; this records what the implementer understood.

The two-scale minimum is the reflection evidence rule pointed at patterns. One observation is an anecdote, and a log that accepts anecdotes fills with profundities and stops being read. minItems on `scales` is that rule made checkable.

Patterns are NOT subjects and carry no URN. They are addressed by ledger id and filename. Whether they should become subjects classified by facets is open - see ledger 0004.

ledger.description: The ledger id of the iteration that recorded this pattern, and the filename prefix. Not a date and not a version: two iterations can land on one day and dates do not order them, while the ledger id already increments and already ties to an annotated tag.

tag.description: The annotated git tag the recording iteration was sealed with.

scales.description: Where the shape was observed, two or more, each a name a reader can go and look up - a function, a file, a rule. Prose belongs in the body's 'Where it was seen' section. Short and comma-free because the store's front-matter grammar splits inline lists on the comma; a scale needing a sentence is a scale that has not been located yet.

confidence.description: Required, and never defaults to 1 - the same rule the store applies to assignments. A shape seen twice and named once is not a law. If you are tempted to write 1 because you have nothing better, the honest value is lower and the body should say why.

supersedes.description: Pattern ids this one subsumes or corrects. Renames never delete, so a superseded pattern stays on disk and stays resolvable.
